To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) renal innervation appears during fetal life, but is not an essential regulator of renal hemodynamics during resting conditions; (2) RNS causes renal vasoconstriction in adult animals, but renal vasodilation during alpha-adrenoceptors blockade in fetal and newborn lambs; (3) the RAS is an important regulator of renal hemodynamic and function during fetal life; and (4) the RAS plays a role in the development of hypertension during fetal life.
renal innervation and the renin- angiotensin system are important modulators of renal hemodynamics during development.
the renal neurohormonal system is important in the regulation of renal function and hemodynamics in fetal and newborn, but not adult, sheep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the RNS and RAS during fetal and postnatal maturnation in sheep.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system and RAS in modulating fetal and neonatal renal function.
the regulation of fetal renal function and its relationship to fetal and postnatal cardiovascular function and growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fetal kidney has a high degree of autonomy, and that the neurohormonal systems have a relatively minor role in the regulation of fetal renal function during resting conditions.

the neurohormonal system plays an important role during fetal life and in the immediate newborn period in the maintenance of renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate, but that its role in modulating renal function during postnatal maturation and in the adult is less important.
renal innervation is present early during fetal life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neurohormonal system plays a minor role during resting conditions in the regulation of fetal renal function but may be important in the control of fetal renal blood flow and renal function during stress.
the neurohormonal regulation is different during development than in adults.
the fetal and postnatal kidney is a highly regulated system that undergoes significant changes in response to various physiological and pathophysiological stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that

fetal renal innervation is not an important regulator of renal hemodynamics or function in fetal and newborn lambs, but that the RAS is an important modulator during prenatal and postnatally maturation.
the RNS is an important modulator in the control of renal function during the transition to extrauterine life in sheep.
renal innervation does not appear to be a major modulator of renal function and hemodynamics during resting conditions during development.
